node.title: Re: Redirecting Standard Output inside perl
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I'm afraid I don't know what you mean with "STDOUT path = 'c:/users/outputs/out.txt';". But I can answer the general question about how to capture a script's STDOUT from within that script. First, and this has the most limited general usefulness, you can use [doc://select] to change the default output handle for [doc://print] statements.

But probably most useful is [mod://Capture::Tiny], which can capture output not only from the Perl script itself but any external processes it happens to run. Its documentation includes a list of other output-capturing modules, such as ones that use another method for capturing output to a filehandle, [doc://tie]d handles. But I wouldn't necessarily recommend that method either, since it is also not generally applicable (e.g. it won't capture things from external programs run). Update: For the sake of completeness, as another method, the [doc://open] documentation shows how to re-open STDOUT, but this is a fairly low-level operation and again I'd recommend the help of a module here. In any of the aforementioned cases you can of course save the name of the target file in a variable, or perhaps get it from an environment variable via [doc://%ENV] or the command line via e.g. [doc://@ARGV] or [doc://Getopt::Long].
